{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|Out observation, thankfully distant, has been that Jacen Solo became a ''nryghat''&mdash;a monster of nightmares, the sort that haunts the dreams of children. But he was not always so.|Tila Mong, on Darth Caedus|<ref name="Outcast">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast]]''</ref>}}
A '''nryghat''' was a frightening monster that haunted [[Youngling/Legends|children's]] [[Dream/Legends|nightmares]] in the [[Kel Dor (language)/Legends|Kel Dor language]].<ref name="Outcast" /> In [[43 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' places ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast]]'' in [[43 ABY]].</ref> the [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] [[Baran Do]] sage [[Tila Mong]] described the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Darth Caedus]]&mdash;formerly the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Jacen Solo who had fallen to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]&mdash;as a nryghat when discussing with Jedi [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] about the Baran Do techniques that Caedus had learned. Tila Mong contemplated whether his transformation into a being of evil was due to learning such techniques, which may have had a damaging effect on Humans who were otherwise virtuous beings.<ref name="Outcast" />

==Behind the scenes==
The nryghat was introduced in [[2009]]'s ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast]]'', written by [[Aaron Allston]] as the first entry to the ''[[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi]]'' series.<ref name="Outcast" />
